01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 729

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 729
Surah al-Burūj. Meccan; its verses: 22. [Revealed after ash-Shams] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة البروج مكية، وآياتها 22 [نزلت بعد الشمس] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 85:1–3 · Vol. 4, p. 729

Verses 1 to 3

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the heaven containing the constellations (1) And by the Promised Day (2) And by a witness and what is witnessed (3)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ (1) وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ (2) وَشاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ (3)
Vol. 4, p. 729
They are the twelve constellations (burūj), which are the palaces of heaven, by way of simile. It is also said: al-burūj are the stars that are the stations (manāzil) of the moon. It is also said: the great planets/stars; they were called burūj because of their prominence. It is also said: the gates of heaven. “And the Promised Day” is the Day of Resurrection. “And a witness and what is witnessed” means: a witness on that Day and one witnessed on it. What is meant by the witness: whoever bears witness on it among all creatures, and by the witnessed: the wonders of that Day. The manner of their indefiniteness: either what I mentioned regarding His saying “a soul will know what it has brought forth” — as if it were said: “and what is excessive in its abundance of witnesses and witnessed”; or the vagueness in description, as if it were said: “a witness and a witnessed whose description cannot be fathomed.” The statements of the exegetes about them have been confused. It is said: the witness and the witnessed are Muḥammad ﷺ and the Day of Resurrection. It is said: Jesus and his community, because of His saying “and I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them.” It is said: the community of Muḥammad and the other communities. It is said: the Day of Tarwiya and the Day of ʿArafa. It is said: the Day of ʿArafa and Friday. It is said: the Black Stone and the pilgrims. It is said: the days and nights, and the sons of Adam. From al-Ḥasan: there is no day but it proclaims: “I am a new day and I am a witness over what is done in me, so make the most of me; were my sun to set you would not catch me until the Day of Resurrection.” It is said: the recording angels and the sons of Adam. It is said: the prophets and Muḥammad ﷺ.
هي البروج الاثنا عشر، وهي قصور السماء على التشبيه. وقيل: الْبُرُوجِ النجوم التي هي منازل القمر. وقيل: عظام الكواكب. سميت بروجا لظهورها. وقيل: أبواب السماء وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ يوم القيامة وَشاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ يعنى وشاهد في ذلك اليوم ومشهود فيه. والمراد بالشاهد: من يشهد فيه من الخلائق كلهم، وبالمشهود: ما في ذلك اليوم من عجائبه. وطريق تنكيرهما: إما ما ذكرته في قوله عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أَحْضَرَتْ كأنه قيل: وما أفرطت كثرته من شاهد ومشهود. وإما الإبهام في الوصف، كأنه قيل: وشاهد مشهود لا يكتنه وصفهما. وقد اضطربت أقاويل المفسرين فيهما، فقيل: الشاهد والمشهود: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويوم القيامة. وقيل: عيسى. وأمّته. لقوله وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً ما دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ وقيل: أمّة محمد، وسائر الأمم: وقيل: يوم التروية، ويوم عرفة. وقيل: يوم عرفة، ويوم الجمعة. وقيل. الحجر الأسود، والحجيج. وقيل: الأيام والليالي، وبنو آدم. وعن الحسن: ما من يوم إلا وينادى: إنى يوم جديد وإنى على ما يعمل فىّ شهيد، فاغتمنى، فلو غابت شمسي لم تدركني إلى يوم القيامة: وقيل: الحفظة وبنو آدم. وقيل: الأنبياء ومحمد عليه السلام.
03
Q 85:4–9 · Vol. 4, pp. 729–732

Verses 4 to 9

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Destroyed were the companions of the trench (4) The fire full of fuel (5) When they were sitting by it (6) And they, to what they were doing against the believers, were witnesses (7) And they resented them not except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy (8) To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and God is, over all things, Witness (9)
قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ (4) النَّارِ ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ (5) إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْها قُعُودٌ (6) وَهُمْ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ (7) وَما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ (8) الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (9)
Vol. 4, p. 729
Question
If you ask: where is the answer to the oath?
فإن قلت: أين جواب القسم؟
Answer
I say: it is omitted, indicated by His saying “Destroyed were the companions of the trench,” as if it were said: “I swear by these things that they are accursed” — meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh — “as the companions of the trench were cursed”; and that
قلت: محذوف يدل عليه قوله قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ كأنه قيل: أقسم بهذه الأشياء أنهم ملعونون، يعنى كفار قريش كما لعن أصحاب الأخدود، وذلك
Vol. 4, p. 730
is because the sura came to strengthen the believers and make them steadfast against the harm of the people of Mecca, and to remind them of what befell those before them: torment on account of faith, the infliction of kinds of harm, and their patience and steadfastness, so that they would take comfort in them and bear what they were encountering from their people, and know that their disbelievers are with God in the position of those tormented ones burned with fire — accursed, deserving that it be said of them: “Quraysh were destroyed,” as it was said: “the companions of the trench were destroyed.” And “qutila” is an imprecation against them, as in His saying “Destroyed is man, how ungrateful he is!” It is also read “qattila,” with shadda. Al-ukhdūd is the groove in the earth, which is a cleft; its like in form and meaning are al-khaqq and al-ukhqūq; from it [the saying]: “his legs sank into the burrows of rats” [1]. It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: A certain king had a sorcerer; when he grew old he attached to him a boy to teach him sorcery; and on the boy's way was a monk; he listened to him; and one day on his way he saw a beast that had halted the people. He took a stone and said: “O God, if the monk is dearer to You than the sorcerer, kill it,” and it killed it. After that the boy used to heal the born-blind and the leper and cure illnesses; a companion of the king went blind and he cured him, and the king regained sight [through the boy's doing] and asked him: “Who restored your sight?” He said: “My Lord.” The king was angry and tortured him. He pointed to the boy, and he tortured him; he pointed to the monk, who would not go back on his religion, so he was split with a saw. The boy refused [to recant], so he was taken to a mountain to be thrown from its summit; he prayed, and the mountain shook the people so they fell down, and he was saved; then he was taken to a qurqūr [2] and they went out to deep water to drown him; he prayed, and the ship capsized with them, and they drowned and he was saved. He said to the king: “You will not kill me until you gather the people on one plain, crucify me on a palm trunk, take an arrow from my quiver and say: ‘In the name of God, the Lord of the boy,’ then shoot me with it.” He shot him and it landed in his temple; he put his hand on it and died. The people said: “We believe in the Lord of the boy.” It was said to the king: “What you feared has befallen you.” So he ordered trenches at the mouths of the lanes, and fires were kindled in them, and whoever of them did not go back he threw into them, until a woman came with a child, and she hung back [3] from falling in; the child said: “O mother, be patient, for you are on the truth,” so she plunged in. It is also said: he said to her, “Fall in and do not be hypocritical.” It is also said: he said to her, “It is only a moment's closing of the eye,” so she was patient [4]. And from ʿAlī ؓ: that when they differed on the rulings concerning the Magians he said: They are People of a Book and they used to hold fast to their Book; wine had been made lawful to them; one of their kings took it and got drunk and fell upon his sister; when he sobered he regretted it and sought a way out, and she said to him: “The way out is that you address the people and say, ‘O people, God has made marriage to sisters lawful,’ then address them afterward and say, ‘God has forbidden it.’” He addressed them and they did not accept it from him
أن السورة وردت في تثبيت المؤمنين وتصبيرهم على أذى أهل مكة، وتذكيرهم بما جرى على من تقدّمهم: من التعذيب على الإيمان. وإلحاق أنواع الأذى، وصبرهم وثباتهم، حتى يأنسوا بهم ويصبروا على ما كانوا يلقون من قومهم، ويعلموا أن كفارهم عند الله بمنزلة أولئك المعذبين المحرقين بالنار، ملعونون أحقاء بأن يقال فيهم: قتلت قريش، كما قيل: قتل أصحاب الأخدود وقتل: دعاء عليهم، كقوله قُتِلَ الْإِنْسانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ وقرئ: قتل، بالتشديد. والأخدود: الخدّ في الأرض وهو الشق، ونحوهما بناء ومعنى: الخق والأخقوق. ومنه فساخت قوائمه في أخاقيق جرذان «1» . روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: كان لبعض الملوك ساحر، فلما كبر ضمّ إليه غلاما ليعلمه السحر، وكان في طريق الغلام راهب: فسمع منه، فرأى في طريقه ذات يوم دابة قد حبست الناس. فأخذ حجرا فقال: اللهم إن كان الراهب أحبّ إليك من الساحر فاقتلها، فقتلها، فكان الغلام بعد ذلك يبرئ الأكمه والأبرص، ويشفى من الأدواء، وعمى جليس للملك فأبرأه فأبصره الملك فسأله فقال: من ردّ عليك بصرك؟ فقال: ربى، فغضب فعذبه. فدل على الغلام فعذبه، فدل على الراهب، فلم يرجع الراهب عن دينه، فقدّ بالمنشار وأبى الغلام فذهب به إلى جبل ليطرح من ذروته، فدعا فرجب بالقوم، فطاحوا ونجا، فذهب به إلى قرقور «2» فلججوا به ليغرقوه، فدعا فانكفأت بهم السفينة، فغرقوا ونجا، فقال للملك: لست بقاتلي حتى تجمع الناس في صعيد وتصلبني على جذع وتأخذ سهما من كنانتي وتقول: بسم الله رب الغلام، ثم ترميني به. فرماه فوقع في صدغه فوضع يده عليه ومات، فقال الناس: آمنا برب الغلام، فقيل للملك. نزل بك ما كنت تحذر، فأمر بأخاديد في أفواه السكك وأو قدت فيها النيران فمن لم يرجع منهم طرحه فيها حتى جاءت امرأة معها صبى فتقاعست «3» أن تقع فيها، فقال الصبى: يا أماه، اصبري فإنك على الحق، فاقتحمت. وقيل: قال لها قعى ولا تنافقى. وقيل: قال لها ما هي إلا غميضة فصبرت «4» . وعن على رضى الله عنه: أنهم حين اختلفوا في أحكام المجوس قال: هم أهل كتاب وكانوا متمسكين بكتابهم، وكانت الخمر قد أحلت لهم، فتناولها بعض ملوكهم فسكر، فوقع على أخته فلما صحا ندم وطلب المخرج، فقالت له: المخرج أن تخطب الناس فتقول: يا أيها الناس، إنّ الله أحل نكاح الأخوات، ثم تخطبهم بعد ذلك فتقول: إن الله حرّمه، فخطب فلم يقبلوا منه
Vol. 4, p. 731
and she said to him: “Spread the whip among them,” and they did not accept; she said to him: “Spread the sword among them,” and they did not accept; so she ordered him [to make] trenches and kindle fires and to throw into them whoever refused; they are the ones whom God intended by His saying “Destroyed were the companions of the trench” [1]. It is also said: a man of those who were upon the religion of Jesus ﷺ came to Najrān and called them, and they responded; Dhū Nuwās the Jew marched against them with troops from Ḥimyar, and gave them a choice between the fire and Judaism; they refused, so he burned twelve thousand of them in the trenches. It is also said: seventy thousand [2]; and it is mentioned that the length of the trench was forty cubits and its width twelve cubits [3]. From the Prophet ﷺ: that when the companions of the trench were mentioned he would seek refuge from the hardship of trial [4]. “The fire” is a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) for “the trench”; “full of fuel” describes it as a great fire having what raises its flame, of abundant firewood and people's bodies; it is read “al-wuqūd” with ḍamma. “When” is a temporal adverb of “were destroyed,” i.e., they were cursed when they surrounded the fire, sitting around it. The meaning of “ʿalayhā” is: upon what approaches it of the edges of the trench, as in the line: “And the generous one and al-Muḥalliq passed the night over the fire” [5]; and as you say “I passed over him,” meaning: being on top of a place close to him. The meaning of their witnessing the burning of the believers: they were commissioned with that and made witnesses, each testifying for the other before the king that none of them had been remiss in what he was ordered and entrusted with of torture. It is also possible that what is meant is: they are witnesses to what they do to the believers, and will give their testimony on the Day of Resurrection — “the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them about what they used to do.” “And they resented them not” — they did not find fault with them nor denounce anything except faith, as in the line: “And there is no fault in them except that their swords …” [6]. Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said: “They resented nothing in the Banū Umayya except / that they are forbearing when they are angry” [7]
فقالت له: ابسط فيهم السوط، فلم يقبلوا، فقالت له: ابسط فيهم السيف، فلم يقبلوا، فأمرته بالأخاديد وإيقاد النيران وطرح من أبى فيها، فهم الذين أرادهم الله بقوله قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ «1» وقيل: وقع إلى نجران رجل ممن كان على دين عيسى عليه السلام، فدعاهم فأجابوه فسار إليهم ذو نواس اليهودي بجنود من حمير، فخيرهم بين النار واليهودية فأبوا، فأحرق منهم اثنى عشر ألفا في الأخاديد. وقيل: سبعين ألفا «2» ، وذكر أنّ طول الأخدود: أربعون ذراعا وعرضه اثنا عشر ذراعا «3» . وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان إذا ذكر أصحاب الأخدود تعوّذ من جهد البلاء «4» النَّارِ بدل اشتمال من الأخدود ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ وصف لها بأنها نار عظيمة لها ما يرتفع به لهبها من الحطب الكثير وأبدان الناس، وقرئ: الوقود، بالضم إِذْ ظرف لقتل، أى لعنوا حين أحدقوا بالنار قاعدين حولها. ومعنى عَلَيْها على ما يدنو منها من حافات الأخدود، كقوله: وبات على النّار النّدى والمحلّق «5» وكما تقول: مرت عليه، تريد: مستعليا لمكان يدنو منه، ومعنى شهادتهم على إحراق المؤمنين: أنهم وكلوا بذلك وجعلوا شهودا يشهد بعضهم لبعض عند الملك أنّ أحدا منهم لم يفرط فيما أمر به وفوض إليه من التعذيب. ويجوز أن يراد: أنهم شهود على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين، يؤدّون شهادتهم يوم القيامة يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ. وَما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ وما عابوا منهم وما أنكروا إلا الإيمان، كقوله: ولا عيب فيهم غير أنّ سيوفهم «6» قال ابن الرقيات: ما نقموا من بنى أميّة إلّا … أنّهم يحلمون إن غضبوا «7»
Vol. 4, p. 732
Abū Ḥaywa read “naqimū” with kasra; the eloquent form is the fatḥa. And He mentioned the attributes by which He deserves to be believed in and worshipped, namely being “the Exalted in Might” — overpowering, able, whose punishment is feared — and “the Praiseworthy” — beneficent, due praise for His favour, and whose reward is hoped for. “To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth”: so everyone in them is bound to worship Him and be humble before Him — as an estimation — because what they resented in them [the believers] is the truth that none resents but a man of falsehood immersed in error, and the resenters are fit for God's vengeance upon them with a punishment to which none is equal. “And God is, over all things, Witness” is a threat to them, meaning that He knows what they did and will requite them for it.
وقرأ أبو حيوة: نقموا، بالكسر، والفصيح: هو الفتح. وذكر الأوصاف التي يستحق بها أن يؤمن به ويعبد، وهو كونه عزيزا غالبا قادرا يخشى عقابه حميدا منعما. يجب له الحمد على نعمته ويرجى ثوابه لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فكل من فيهما تحق عليه عبادته والخشوع له تقديرا، لأن ما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ هو الحق الذي لا ينقمه إلا مبطل منهمك في الغىّ، وإن الناقمين أهل لانتقام الله منهم بعذاب لا يعدله عذاب وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ وعيد لهم، يعنى أنه علم ما فعلوا، وهو مجازيهم عليه.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 730
1. (1) . His statement “juradhān”: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, “al-jurdh” is a kind of rat; plural: al-juradhān. (ʿ)
2. . His statement “qurqūr”: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, “al-qurqūr” is the long ship. (ʿ)
3. . His statement “fa-taqāʿasat”: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, “taqāʿasa” when one holds back from a matter and does not advance. (ʿ) [.....]
4. . Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Ṭabarī, al-Ṭabarānī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Abū Yaʿlā and al-Bazzār all reported it, from the transmission of Ibn Abī Laylā, by [various] routes, the closest of them to the wording of the book being the narrative of al-Ṭabarī. Thābit al-Bunānī was alone in transmitting it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
1. (1) . قوله «جرذان» في الصحاح «الجرذ» : ضرب من الفأر والجمع: الجرذان. (ع)
2. . قوله «قرقور» في الصحاح «القرقور» : السفينة الطويلة. (ع)
3. . قوله «فتقاعست» في الصحاح «تقاعس» : إذا تأخر عن الأمر ولم يتقدم. (ع) [.....]
4. . أخرجه مسلم. والترمذي والنسائي وابن حبان والطبري والطبراني وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو يعلى والبزار كلهم من رواية ابن أبى ليلى من طرق وأقربها إلى لفظ الكتاب سياق الطبري. تفرد به ثابت البناني عن عبد الرحمن.
Vol. 4, p. 731
1. (1) . Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ṭabarī, al-Ṭabarānī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq and al-Bazzār all reported it, from the transmission of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥumayd, and al-Ṭabarī from the transmission of Jaʿfar ibn Abī l-Mughīra from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, who said: “When the Muslims defeated the people of al-Asfīdhiyān they withdrew, and [ʿUmar] ؓ came to them. They gathered and said: What rulings apply to the Magians? They are not People of the Book, and they are not among the polytheists of the Arabs. He said: They are People of the Book.” And he mentioned it. The narrative of al-Ṭabarī is more complete than it.
2. . Ibn Isḥāq reported it in the Sīra: Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb; and he mentioned it at length.
3. . Al-Thaʿlabī transmitted it from al-Kalbī.
4. . Ibn Abī Shayba reported it from Abū Usāma from ʿAwf from al-Ḥasan thus.
5. . The explanation of this line was given in Part Three, page 53; refer to it if you wish. End of the corrector's note.
6. . The explanation of this line was given in Part Two, page 142; refer to it if you wish. End of the corrector's note.
7. . By Qays al-Ruqayyāt. “Naqamū” means they disliked; and ḥalima — like ẓarufa — means he forgave. He says: they made the finest of things, which is forbearance at the time of anger, ugly. It is possible that the subject of both verbs is a pronoun for the Banū Umayya; and it is possible that the first is for them and the second for those who resented. In it is the following-up of praise with what resembles blame, to exaggerate the praise, since he made forbearance at anger a matter of blame, when it is the ultimate in praise. It is also reported “mā naqima l-nās,” and according to it the correct thing is to drop “bayn” [as printed] for the sake of the metre.
1. (1) . أخرجه مسلم والترمذي والنسائي وأبو يعلى. والطبري والطبراني. وأحمد وإسحاق والبزار كلهم من رواية عبد الرحمن بن حميد والطبري من رواية جعفر بن أبى المغيرة عن عبد الرحمن بن أيزى قال «لما هزم المسلمون أهل الاسفيذيان انصرفوا فجاءهم يعنى عمر رضى الله عنه. فاجتمعوا فقالوا. أى شيء يجرى على المجوس من الأحكام؟ نهم ليسوا أهل كتاب. وليسوا من مشركي العرب. فقال: هم أهل الكتاب. فذكره. وسياق الطبري أتم منه
2. . أخرجه ابن إسحاق في السيرة، حدثني يزيد بن أبى زياد عن محمد بن كعب. فذره مطولا.
3. . نقله الثعلبي عن الكلبي.
4. . أخرجه ابن أبى شيبة عن أبى أسامة عن عوف عن الحسن بهذا.
5. . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الثالث صفحة 53 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
6. . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الثاني صفحة 142 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
7. . لقيس الرقيات. ونقموا كرهوا: وحلم- كظرف-: صفح. يقول: إنهم جعلوا أحسن الأشياء وهو الحلم عند الغضب قبيحا. ويجوز أن فاعل الفعلين ضمير بنى أمية. ويجوز أن الأول لهم، والثاني: الناقمين. وفيه استتباع المدح بما يشبه الذم للمبالغة في المدح، حيث جعل الحلم عند الغضب ذما، مع أنه غاية في المدح. ويروى ما نقم الناس، وعليها فالصواب إسقاط «بين» لأجل الوزن.
04
Q 85:10–11 · Vol. 4, p. 732

Verses 10 to 11

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent — for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning (10) Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow; that is the great attainment (11)
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَلَهُمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ (10) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ (11)
Vol. 4, p. 732
It is possible that by “those who persecuted” He means specifically the companions of the trench, and by “those who believed” those thrown into the trench. The meaning of “fatanūhum”: they tormented them with fire and burned them. “For them in the Hereafter is the punishment of Hell” because of their disbelief, “and for them is the punishment of the Burning” — which is another great fire that spreads as a conflagration spreads, in return for their burning the believers; or: for them is the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter and for them is the punishment of the Burning in this world, because it is reported that the fire turned back upon them and burned them. It is also possible that He means: those who persecuted the believers, i.e., afflicted them with harm in general, and the believers: those persecuted; and that for the persecutors there are two punishments in the Hereafter: for their disbelief and for their persecution.
ويجوز أن يريد بالذين فتنوا: أصحاب الأخدود خاصة، وبالذين آمنوا: المطروحين في الأخدود. ومعنى فتنوهم: عذبوهم بالنار وأحرقوهم فَلَهُمْ في الآخرة عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ بكفرهم وَلَهُمْ عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ وهي نار أخرى عظيمة تتسع كما يتسع الحريق بإحراقهم المؤمنين. أو لهم عذاب جهنم في الآخرة، ولهم عذاب الحريق في الدنيا، لما روى أن النار انقلبت عليهم فأحرقتهم. ويجوز أن يريد: الذين فتنوا المؤمنين، أى: بلوهم بالأذى على العموم، والمؤمنين: المفتونين، وأن للفاتنين عذابين في الآخرة: لكفرهم، ولفتنتهم.
05
Q 85:12–16 · Vol. 4, pp. 732–733

Verses 12 to 16

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe (12) Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats (13) And He is the Forgiving, the Loving (14) Owner of the Throne, the Glorious (15) Doer of what He intends (16)
إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ (12) إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ (13) وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ (14) ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ (15) فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ (16)
Vol. 4, p. 732
Al-baṭsh is seizing with violence; so when it is described as severe, it is doubled and intensified: it is His seizing of tyrants and wrongdoers, taking them with punishment and vengeance. “Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats” — that is, He originates the seizure and repeats it, meaning: He seizes them in this world and in the Hereafter. Or: He indicated, through His power to originate and repeat, the severity of His seizure. And He threatened the disbelievers that He will repeat them as He originated them, in order to seize them, since they did not give thanks for the favour of origination and denied the repetition.
البطش: الأخذ بالعنف، فإذا وصف بالشدة فقد تضاعف وتفاقم: وهو بطشه بالجبابرة والظلمة، وأخذهم بالعذاب والانتقام إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ أى يبدئ البطش ويعيده، يعنى: يبطش بهم في الدنيا وفي الآخرة. أو دل باقتداره على الإبداء والاعادة على شدة بطشه. وأوعد الكفرة بأنه يعيدهم كما أبدأهم ليبطش بهم إذ لم يشكروا نعمة الإبداء وكذبوا بالاعادة.
Vol. 4, p. 733
It is read “yabdaʾu.” “Al-Wadūd”: the one who does for those who obey Him what the loving one does: giving them what they want. It is read “dhī l-ʿarshi” as an attribute of “your Lord.” It is read “al-majīdi” in the genitive, as an attribute of the Throne. The majd of God is His greatness; the majd of the Throne is its height and greatness. “Faʿʿāl” is the predicate of an omitted subject. It was said “faʿʿāl” only because what He wills and does is extremely abundant [1].
وقرئ: يبدأ الْوَدُودُ الفاعل بأهل طاعته ما يفعله الودود: من إعطائهم ما أرادوا. وقرئ: ذى العرش، صفة لربك. وقرئ: المجيد، بالجر صفة للعرش. ومجد الله: عظمته. ومجد العرش: علوه وعظمته فَعَّالٌ خبر مبتدأ محذوف. وإنما قيل: فعال، لأنّ ما يريد ويفعل في غاية الكثرة «1» .
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 733
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “It was said ‘faʿʿāl’ only because what He wills and does is extremely abundant.” Aḥmad said: He did not esteem God with His true estimation! Why did he not say: “He has no agent but Him”? And is the one who opposes that anything but a polytheist? And how many acts has God Exalted willed, on the belief of the Qadariyya, and not done? Suppose we set aside consideration of the requirement of the intensiveness of the form: has He not indicated by His saying “li-mā yurīd” the generality of His act in all that He wills? So returning it to specificity is nothing but a retreat from the texts.
2. . His statement “wa-l-lawḥ al-hawāʾ”: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, “al-lawḥ,” with ḍamma, is the air between heaven and earth. (ʿ)
3. . Al-Wāḥidī, al-Thaʿlabī and Ibn Mardawayh reported it with their chain to [Ubayy] ibn Kaʿb [as printed: “ibn Kaʿb”].
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إنما يقال فعال لأن ما يريد ويفعل في غاية الكثرة» قال أحمد: ما قدر الله حق قدره، هلا قال: إنه لا فاعل إلا هو، وهل المخالف لذلك إلا مشرك، وكم أراد الله تعالى على معتقد القدرية من فعل فلم يفعله، وهب أنا طرحنا النظر في مقتضى مبالغة الصيغة، أليس قد دل بقوله لِما يُرِيدُ على عموم فعله في جميع مراده، فما رده إلى الخصوص إلا نكوص عن النصوص.
2. . قوله «واللوح الهواء» في الصحاح «اللوح» بالضم: الهواء بين السماء والأرض. (ع)
3. . أخرجه الواحدي والثعلبي وابن مردويه باسنادهم إلى بن كعب.
06
Q 85:17–22 · Vol. 4, p. 733

Verses 17 to 22

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Has there come to you the story of the soldiers (17) Pharaoh and Thamūd? (18) But those who disbelieved are in denial (19) And God encompasses them from behind (20) But it is a glorious Qurʾān (21) In a preserved tablet (22)
هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ الْجُنُودِ (17) فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ (18) بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي تَكْذِيبٍ (19) وَاللَّهُ مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ (20) بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ (21) فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ (22)
Vol. 4, p. 733
“Pharaoh and Thamūd” is a substitution for the soldiers. By Pharaoh He meant him and his people, as in “from Pharaoh and their chiefs.” The meaning: you have known the denial of those soldiers of the messengers and what befell them because of their denial; “but those who disbelieved” of your people “are in denial” — what a denial! — and a deserving of punishment; and God knows their conditions and has power over them, and they cannot frustrate Him. “Encompassing them from behind” is a figure that they cannot escape Him, just as what is surrounded cannot escape from what surrounds it. The meaning of the “but” [iḍrāb]: that their affair is more remarkable than the affair of those, because they heard of their stories and of what happened to them, and saw the traces of their destruction and took no lesson, and denied more intensely than their denial. “But it” — i.e., but this which they denied — “is a glorious Qurʾān”: noble, of lofty rank among the books and in its composition and inimitability. It is also read “Qurʾānu majīdin,” by annexation, i.e., “the Qurʾān of a Glorious [Lord].” Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read “fī lawḥ.” Al-lawḥ is the air [2], meaning [the space] above the seventh heaven, in which is the Tablet, “preserved” from the reaching of devils to it. It is read “maḥfūẓun,” with raising, as an attribute of the Qurʾān. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Whoever recites Sūrat al-Burūj, God will give him ten good deeds for the number of every Friday and every Day of ʿArafa that occurs in this world” [3].
فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ بدل من الجنود. وأراد بفرعون إياه وآله، كما في قوله مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِمْ والمعنى: قد عرفت تكذيب تلك الجنود الرسل وما نزل بهم لتكذيبهم بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا من قومك فِي تَكْذِيبٍ أىّ: تكذيب واستيجاب للعذاب، والله عالم بأحوالهم وقادر عليهم وهم لا يعجزونه. والاحاطة بهم من ورائهم: مثل لأنهم لا يفوتونه، كما لا يفوت فائت الشيء المحيط به. ومعنى الاضراب: أن أمرهم أعجب من أمر أولئك، لأنهم سمعوا بقصصهم وبما جرى عليهم، ورأوا آثار هلاكهم ولم يعتبروا، وكذبوا أشد من تكذيبهم بَلْ هُوَ أى بل هذا الذي كذبوا به قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ شريف عالى الطبقة في الكتب وفي نظمه وإعجازه. وقرئ: قرآن مجيد، بالاضافة، أى: قرآن رب مجيد. وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر: في لوح. واللوح: الهواء «2» ، يعنى: اللوح فوق السماء السابعة الذي فيه اللوح مَحْفُوظٍ من وصول الشياطين إليه. وقرئ: محفوظ، بالرفع صفة القرآن. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة البروج أعطاه الله بعدد كل يوم جمعة وكل يوم عرفة يكون في الدنيا عشر حسنات «3» » .
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 733
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “It was said ‘faʿʿāl’ only because what He wills and does is extremely abundant.” Aḥmad said: He did not esteem God with His true estimation! Why did he not say: “He has no agent but Him”? And is the one who opposes that anything but a polytheist? And how many acts has God Exalted willed, on the belief of the Qadariyya, and not done? Suppose we set aside consideration of the requirement of the intensiveness of the form: has He not indicated by His saying “li-mā yurīd” the generality of His act in all that He wills? So returning it to specificity is nothing but a retreat from the texts.
2. . His statement “wa-l-lawḥ al-hawāʾ”: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, “al-lawḥ,” with ḍamma, is the air between heaven and earth. (ʿ)
3. . Al-Wāḥidī, al-Thaʿlabī and Ibn Mardawayh reported it with their chain to [Ubayy] ibn Kaʿb [as printed: “ibn Kaʿb”].
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إنما يقال فعال لأن ما يريد ويفعل في غاية الكثرة» قال أحمد: ما قدر الله حق قدره، هلا قال: إنه لا فاعل إلا هو، وهل المخالف لذلك إلا مشرك، وكم أراد الله تعالى على معتقد القدرية من فعل فلم يفعله، وهب أنا طرحنا النظر في مقتضى مبالغة الصيغة، أليس قد دل بقوله لِما يُرِيدُ على عموم فعله في جميع مراده، فما رده إلى الخصوص إلا نكوص عن النصوص.
2. . قوله «واللوح الهواء» في الصحاح «اللوح» بالضم: الهواء بين السماء والأرض. (ع)
